review: I read the lyrics before I play anything to my children; I have done so for four years and it has cost me a great many albums. This one I checked twice and then played twice. "Nachamu, Nachamu, Ami" sets Isaiah 40 without softening it, and "Every Valley Lifted" resists the temptation to make the comfort arrive before the wilderness has been named — which is precisely what the text does and precisely what almost every modern setting of it fails to do. My fourteen-year-old asked me what the Hebrew meant. That is the first question she has asked me about scripture in some months, and I did not have to manufacture it.

review: I want to be precise, because four stars from me is not a dismissal. The craftsmanship is high and "Daniel Prayed Toward Jerusalem" is excellent. My reservation is with the framing of the album as a whole: it moves at points from recovering the Hebraic context of the text — which I support entirely — toward implying that context is required for right standing, which my confession does not hold and which I do not think the album quite intends. I would still play it. I would want to be sitting beside my children when I did. Written respectfully, and with real appreciation for the work.
